spec.title: PROP-075 — Template packages and version management for every application
spec.p: Framework record, owner request 2026-11-09; design settled 2026-11-10 against the tree at `7d495d137`. Status `impl/work`: the shape of sections 1–5 is decided by the owner; the details below section 6 are the design settled at planning time against the actual code, and implementation follows the corporate-environment campaign (campaign node `APP-VERSIONS`, after `CORP-ENV`, before `SYS-PROMPT`). The owner chose this order deliberately: the feature is user-facing and crosses many surfaces (manifest, resolver, registry, mirror, artifact drops, installer, alternatives, PATH, shells, projects), so it doubles as an end-to-end test of them. The implementation plan is `campaigns/app-versions-2026-11/PLAN.md`. **Phases P1, P5a, P2, P3 and P5b are implemented (2026-11-10):** the manifest spelling, the typed `[template]` section with its refusals, the whole variable grammar and the pure renderer `crates/vibe-template` (P1); version files, `vibe app env`, `vibe hook` and `vibe app exec` (P5a); resolution, channels, the lock record, trust and the offline cache (P2); `org.vibevm.node/node` itself as one template package with the generator retired (P3); and `vibe app versions` (P5b). The as-built records of those phases are `#P2-AS-BUILT`, `#P5A-AS-BUILT`, `#P3-AS-BUILT` and `#P5B-AS-BUILT`. Phase **P4** is implemented too, in its three commits: the mirror's declarative selection, its template snapshot, the payload projection with its budget and `--dry-run` counts, and `--prune` with its plan — so every fact of section 3 is `impl/done` and `#P4-AS-BUILT` records what they decided. Phase **P7a** is implemented too (2026-11-10): the `keyed` version-file format with `tool-versions` as its short spelling, and `--write-version-file` for both formats, so `#VERSION-FILE-KEYED` and `#VERSION-FILE-WRITE` are `impl/done` and `#P7A-AS-BUILT` records what they decided. Phase **P7b** is implemented too (2026-11-10): the `[[application.ecosystem]]` declaration with its four verbs and the argv-only item contract, the recommends shorthand as synthesised installer features, the synthesised `ecosystem:<id>` migration entry, the run record and its kept work directory, and the explicit `vibe app extras list|remove|self-upgrade` verbs — so `#ECOSYSTEM-RECOMMENDS`, `#ECOSYSTEM-MIGRATION` and `#PACKAGE-ACTIONS` are `impl/done` and `#P7B-AS-BUILT` records what they decided. Phase **P7c** is implemented too (2026-11-10): the user's own `[slot.<slot>.extras.<ecosystem>]` list in `~/.vibe/config.toml`, the final-list arithmetic over it, the apply after an `install -g` / `update -g` that places a **new** version of a slot, `--no-extras`, `vibe app extras apply|add|drop|import`, and the per-adapter installation record as optional members of the generation P7d paid for — so the last two clauses close and `#ECOSYSTEM-ADAPTER` and `#SLOT-EXTRAS` are `impl/done`, with `#P7C-AS-BUILT` recording what the code decided. Phase **P7f** is implemented too (2026-11-11), in both halves: the differential conformance suite of `conformance/vibenvm/` and the `org.vibevm.node/vibenvm` shim it compares against, with the npm ecosystem adapter and the two version files the shim needs added to `org.vibevm.node/node` at template revision 1.1.0 — so **every fact of section 5 is `impl/done`**, the proof is a measured verdict of 0 over nine cases and all 52 required `(subcommand, flag)` pairs rather than a promise, and `#P7F-AS-BUILT` records what the shim needed. The campaign's **close-out** is implemented too (2026-11-11): the four shortfalls P7f found (`BACKLOG.md#b-262`…`#b-265`) are closed as one design — `#VERSION-FILE-VALUE`, a version file's value read the way every switcher reads its own file, with `#VERSION-FILE-FORMATS`, `#VERSION-FILE-WRITE` and `#VERSIONS-LIST-OUTPUT` amended for the install, the third home of `--write-version-file` and the version pattern — and PLAN §7's whole-campaign `campaigns/app-versions-2026-11/accept.sh` exists and passes all thirteen legs; `#P7-CLOSE-AS-BUILT` records what that decided. The two general features that belong to the package model and live elsewhere are recorded in their own documents: PROP-077 (`[recommends]` on applications and the general `--no-recommends`) and PROP-065 `#ordinary-reach` (multi-step installation for ordinary packages).

p.VERSIONS-PURPOSE: vibe is a version manager for every application, not one per tool: what nvm does for Node (and pyenv, sdkman, rbenv for others) vibe does for any application package, the way mise and asdf do it with plugins. The general machinery lives in vibe; everything specific to one tool (where its versions are listed, its version files, how its state moves between versions) lives in that tool's package.

p.TEMPLATE-FLAG: A template package declares itself explicitly in its manifest (`[package] template = true`); the property is never inferred from a version spelling (`0.0.0`, a `-TEMPLATE` suffix) or from a repository name. The package's own `version` is the revision of the template, independent of the versions it produces, so a template can be fixed and extended without touching any produced version.

p.TEMPLATE-VERSIONS: `[template.versions]` names where the produced versions come from: a closed set of source kinds (a JSON document with a selector, an explicit list, later others), an optional prefix strip and lower bound. `[template.digests]` names where the SHA-256 of every input comes from (for example a `SHASUMS256.txt` per version); a template without a digest source is refused.

p.TEMPLATE-VARIABLES: The rest of the manifest is written once with variables: `{version}`, `{major}`, `{minor}`, `{patch}`, `{platform}`, `{arch}`, fields of the version's record from the source (`{meta.NAME}`) and `{sha256:FILE}` from the digest source. Rendering is a pure function of the template, the version record and the digests; the rendered manifest is an ordinary manifest validated by the ordinary rules.

p.TEMPLATE-RESOLUTION: A template's version domain joins the resolver as the versions its source lists plus any concretely published versions of the same package; a concrete version wins over the template's rendering of the same version, so one version can be fixed by hand. Requirements stay ordinary (`group/name@^22`).

p.TEMPLATE-TRUST: The lock and the installation record carry the template revision, the produced version and the hash of the rendered manifest with its digests. A later rendering of the same version with different digests is an alarm, as a frozen version with changed content is for a mirror. Offline, the last cached version list and digests are used.

p.CHANNELS: `[template.channels]` derives named channels from the version records (for Node: `lts` and `lts/<codename>` from the `lts` field); a requirement may name a channel (`group/name@lts`). Channels are a resolver feature available to concrete packages too (publisher-assigned labels).

p.TEMPLATE-SPELLING: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the exact manifest spelling.** `template = true` is one optional boolean on `[package]`, default `false`, omitted from serialisation when false, so every existing manifest is byte-identical. It joins `PackageMeta` (`crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/package/meta.rs`) and its serde twin `PackageMetaWire` (`…/package/wire.rs`, `deny_unknown_fields`) and both `From` arms. The template's data lives in one new top-level table `[template]`, which must be added to `Manifest` (`…/manifest/document.rs`), to `ManifestWire` (`…/package/visibility.rs`, `deny_unknown_fields`) and to both `TryFrom` arms, or the manifest is refused as an unknown table. `[template]` without `template = true`, and `template = true` without `[template]`, are both validation refusals naming the TOML path, by the rule of PROP-059 `#declaration` that every application-validator refusal names its field as a TOML path. `template = true` is admitted only on `kind = "app"` in this task; other kinds are refused with a message naming the restriction, so the surface can widen later without a format change. A template manifest declares `[compatibility] min_vibe_version` for the vibe that can render it, as any package does.

p.TEMPLATE-SOURCE-KINDS: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the closed source-kind set, deliberately minimal.** `[template.versions] kind` is one of exactly two values to start with. `kind = "json"`: `url` (an HTTPS URL, no template variables — the version list cannot depend on a version), `select` (a selector into the fetched document, see `#TEMPLATE-SELECTOR`), `version_field` (the key of the version string inside each selected record, default `"version"`), optional `strip_prefix` (a literal prefix removed from the version string before it is parsed as semver, `"v"` for Node), optional `min` (an inclusive semver lower bound; versions below it are dropped before anything else sees them), optional `max`, and `prerelease` (`"exclude"`, the default, or `"include"`). `kind = "list"`: one `[[template.versions.item]]` row per version with `version` and an optional free `meta` table, for a tool whose releases are not published as a document. A record whose version string does not parse as semver after `strip_prefix` is **skipped with a reported reason**, never an error, because an upstream index legitimately carries shapes vibe does not understand; a source that yields no usable version at all is an error. The set is closed: a third kind (an HTML listing, a git tag list, an RSS feed) is a later amendment of this fact and a new `kind` value, never an escape hatch — there is no expression language and no scripting of a source, exactly as PROP-065 `#principle` forbids for installers.

p.TEMPLATE-SELECTOR: **Decided 2026-11-10.** `select` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer with one addition: the empty pointer `""` selects the document root. The pointed value must be an array of objects, and each element is one version record; anything else is an error naming the pointer and what was found. Nothing else is a selector — no JSONPath, no filters, no wildcards; a source whose array needs filtering is filtered by `min` / `max` / `prerelease` or by the channel rules, never by the selector. `https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json` needs `select = ""`, `version_field = "version"`, `strip_prefix = "v"`, verified 2026-11-10 against the live document (878 records; each carries `version`, `date`, `files`, `npm`, `v8`, `lts` as `false` or a codename, `security`).

p.TEMPLATE-DIGEST-SOURCE: **Decided 2026-11-10.** `[template.digests] kind` is one of exactly two values. `kind = "sha256sums"`: `url` — an HTTPS URL **template** over the version variables only (`https://nodejs.org/dist/v{version}/SHASUMS256.txt`) — whose body is parsed as `sha256sum(1)` output, one `<digest><space>[*]<name>` pair per line, other lines skipped; a duplicate name is an error. `kind = "json"`: `url` as above plus `select` (a JSON Pointer to an array), `file_field` and `digest_field`, and optional `size_field`, for a release that publishes a JSON checksum manifest. Both kinds may declare `sizes = true` only when they actually carry sizes (`json` with `size_field`); a `{size:FILE}` variable in a template whose digest source carries no sizes is a validation refusal. A template with no `[template.digests]` is refused, as TEMPLATE-VERSIONS states; a digest document is fetched exactly once per produced version and is **immutable** (`#TEMPLATE-CACHE`). Node's upstream publishes digests but not sizes, which is why the current generator takes a hand-made `SIZES` file (`/fast/git/vibe-pkg-node-generator/payload/generate-package-node.py`, `stat -c '%s %n' *`): the Node template therefore omits `size`, and the step panel falls back to the server's `Content-Length`, which PROP-065 `#sizes` and `#display` already allow. That is the one deliberate loss against the generator and it is recorded here so nobody re-discovers it.

p.TEMPLATE-VARIABLE-GRAMMAR: **Decided 2026-11-10 — variables, escaping and typing.** A template is rendered as TOML text to TOML text through `toml_edit`, the crate the manifest layer already uses for comment decoration and codemods (`crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/decor.rs`, `…/manifest/migration.rs`), and the result is then read by the ordinary `Manifest::parse_str`, which is what makes TEMPLATE-VARIABLES' "an ordinary manifest validated by the ordinary rules" literally true. **Substitution happens inside string values only** — never in a key, never in a comment, never in a non-string scalar. The closed variable set is: `{version}` (the produced version, canonical semver), `{version_raw}` (the source's own spelling of it, `v24.22.2` for Node), `{major}`, `{minor}`, `{patch}`, `{prerelease}` (empty when there is none), `{platform}` and `{arch}` (bound, inside an `[[installer_options]]` row and its sub-tables, to that row's own declared `platform` / `arch` ids; referenced anywhere else they are a refusal, because there is nothing to bind them to), `{meta.PATH}` (a dotted path into the version record resolving to a string, number or boolean — an array or object is a refusal naming the path), `{sha256:FILE}` and `{size:FILE}`. `{{` and `}}` are the literal braces; a `{` that opens no known variable is a refusal naming the field as a TOML path, never a silent pass-through. **One level of nesting is allowed and only inside the argument of `sha256:` / `size:`**: `{sha256:node-v{version}-linux-x64.tar.gz}` substitutes the inner variables first, then looks the file up. A declared variable with no value (`{sha256:…}` for a file the digest document does not name) is handled by `#TEMPLATE-OPTION-GATING`. **Typing**: a numeric or boolean field that must vary is written as a string holding exactly one variable and nothing else (`size = "{size:node-v{version}-linux-x64.tar.gz}"`); the renderer replaces the whole TOML node with the typed value. A string that mixes a variable with other text always renders as a string. That one coercion rule is the whole type system; there is no cast syntax. **There is no iteration construct**: the seven Node installer options are written out as seven `[[installer_options]]` rows exactly as the generator emits them today, each naming its own archive literally, because an upstream's own target spelling (`linux-x64`, `darwin-arm64`, `win-x64`) is not vibe's `platform` / `arch` vocabulary and no mapping table would survive the next tool.

p.TEMPLATE-OPTION-GATING: **Decided 2026-11-10 — a version that does not have every target.** Upstream target sets change over time: `node-v{version}-linux-x64-musl.tar.gz` and `node-v{version}-win-arm64.zip` do not exist for every version in Node's index. By default a `{sha256:FILE}` whose file the digest document does not name is a **render error** naming the version, the file and the digest document, because a silently wrong manifest is worse than a refused one. An `[[installer_options]]` row may opt out with `template_optional = true`: such a row is **dropped from the rendered manifest** when any digest variable it references has no value, and the drop is reported by `vibe app versions`, `vibe app describe` and the mirror's dry run with the row id, the version and the missing file. A rendered manifest with no installer option left for the host platform is not an error — it is PROP-059's ordinary "no option for this platform", which `vibe install -g` already reports. A rendered manifest with no installer option at all is a render error. No condition vocabulary over the version record is introduced: `template_optional` plus `min` / `max` cover every case the two real packages need, and a template that needs more waits for a fact amending this one.

p.TEMPLATE-RENDER-LOCATION: **Decided 2026-11-10 — rendering happens at resolution time on the client, always; a registry never renders.** The pure renderer is a new crate `crates/vibe-template` with two modules: `render`, which has no filesystem and no network at all (`render(template_toml: &str, record: &VersionRecord, digests: &DigestTable) -> Result<Rendered>`, where `Rendered` carries the rendered TOML bytes, their SHA-256, the dropped optional rows and the variables consumed), and `source`, which parses `[template]`, parses a fetched version document and a fetched digest document into those pure inputs and knows nothing about where the bytes came from. Fetching, caching, offline policy and store materialisation stay in `vibe-registry` (`#TEMPLATE-DOMAIN-SEAM`). Four reasons rendering is never done at publication, even by a registry that could: (1) `#MIRROR-TEMPLATE-SNAPSHOT` already requires a client inside a closed network to render locally "with the same code as outside", so a server renderer would be a second implementation of the same function whose disagreement with the client's is undetectable — exactly what one pure function exists to prevent; (2) the same fact rejects writing thousands of rendered package directories, which is what publication-time rendering produces; (3) a registry is a `monorepo`, a `localdir`, a bare SSH repository or a plain directory on a share (PROP-002 `#registry-type`, the corporate-env campaign) — none of them has compute, and a feature that worked only on a hosted registry would re-commit Nix's mistake of tying a mechanism to a host, which PROP-002 `#nix-mistakes` names as the thing to avoid; (4) `#TEMPLATE-TRUST` puts the hash of the *rendered* manifest in the lock, so a client that received a rendered manifest would have to render it again to verify the hash — the client renderer exists either way, and a server renderer is pure duplication. A registry and a mirror may cache the *inputs* — the version list and the digest documents, which is exactly what `#MIRROR-SNAPSHOT-LAYOUT` is — and never an output.

p.TEMPLATE-TWO-STAGE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — rendering is two-stage, so a resolution costs one request and an install costs two.** A **skeleton render** uses the version record alone and leaves every digest-bearing field at a declared placeholder; it is enough for everything resolution needs — the package identity, `[compatibility]`, `[requires]`, the installer options' platforms and architectures, the launchers and the public commands — because a digest variable may appear **only** in the digest-bearing fields `steps[].sha256`, `steps[].size`, `installation.sha256`, `installation.size` and `sources[].sha256` / `sources[].size`, and a digest variable anywhere else is a validation refusal naming the TOML path. A **full render** substitutes the digests and is performed only for a version that is actually selected, locked, installed, described or mirrored. A skeleton manifest is validated by the ordinary rules with the digest-bearing fields exempt, is never installed from, never written into a store and never hashed into a lock: the `rendered_sha256` of `#TEMPLATE-LOCK-RECORD` is always the full render's. Consequences, which are the point: enumerating a template's versions is one HTTP request for the whole package (cacheable, `#TEMPLATE-CACHE`); resolving a requirement against it needs zero further requests; installing one version needs exactly one more, for that version's digest document; and a locked install needs no version-list request at all, because the lock already names the version.

p.TEMPLATE-DOCUMENT-READING: **Decided 2026-11-10 while implementing P1 — how a template document is read, what the render rewrites away, and the two places the claim of byte-identity is narrower than it first looked.** (1) **The render rewrites the identity and erases the vocabulary.** `[package].version` becomes the produced version — the template's own `version` is the revision of the template, so no variable spells it and nothing in the template may — and `[package].template`, the whole `[template]` table and every `template_optional` key are removed. The rendered document therefore carries no template vocabulary at all, which is what lets the ordinary `Manifest::parse_str` read it with no knowledge that it was rendered. (2) **The document is read as TOML text, never as a typed `Manifest`.** `#TEMPLATE-VARIABLE-GRAMMAR`'s coercion rule puts a string where a typed field wants a number (`size = "{size:…}"`), so a template that uses it does **not** deserialise into `Manifest`; the renderer parses the text with `toml_edit` and the `[template]` table is deserialised on its own (`vibe_template::template_section`), which is also how a client reads the declaration out of a fetched template package. A template that uses no numeric coercion — both real packages — does deserialise, and then the ordinary validator admits a `{sha256:FILE}` variable in the digest-bearing fields **because `template = true` exempts them**, and refuses it everywhere else; `vibe check`'s template check reads the raw text either way, so neither kind of template is invisible to it. The one consequence worth naming: a template that uses the numeric coercion is reported by `vibe check`'s ordinary manifest-validity cell as unparseable. Admitting a lone variable in a typed numeric field is a later, separate change to the typed layer, and neither real package needs it. (3) **A skeleton's digest placeholder is a declared, valid digest** — sixty-four zeros (`vibe_template::SKELETON_DIGEST`), and `0` for a size — so `#TEMPLATE-TWO-STAGE`'s "validated by the ordinary rules with the digest-bearing fields exempt" is achieved by construction rather than by a second validator, and a placeholder can never be mistaken for a real digest. (4) **`{meta.PATH}` resolves to a string, an integer or a boolean.** A path holding an array, an object, `null` or a **non-integral number** is a refusal naming the path: the declaration stays comparable and a rendered number is exact rather than carrying a float's spelling. (5) **The byte-identity proof against the retired generator holds modulo the generator's four-line provenance header *and* the `size` lines** — the deliberate loss `#TEMPLATE-DIGEST-SOURCE` already records, because nodejs.org publishes digests but no sizes. The golden test strips exactly those and nothing else, and asserts the count of stripped `size` lines, so a second silent divergence cannot hide inside the normalisation.

p.TEMPLATE-DISCOVERY: **Decided 2026-11-10 — how a client learns that `group/name` has a template, and which published version is the revision.** The per-version index record gains one optional boolean `template` (the shared `version_entry` vocabulary, so `primary.jsonl`, `by-name/<name>.json` and the journal carry it transitively), written from the manifest at publish and at index projection. A client asked for the versions of `group/name` therefore splits the index rows in one read: rows with `template = true` are template revisions, every other row is a concrete version. The newest template revision is the **active** template; older revisions stay resolvable by identity so a lock that pins one can be replayed (`#TEMPLATE-LOCK-RECORD`). Having found the active revision, the client fetches that package version through the ordinary path — it needs the whole package tree anyway, since the template's recipes, icons and licence files are the produced version's too — and reads `[template]` from it. For a local-directory registry (`--registry DIR`, `type = "localdir"`, a `monorepo` working copy) the same answer is read from the manifests on disk, which are already local; `vibe_index::layout::project` derives the index from exactly those manifests, so the two paths agree by construction. **A template is therefore discoverable in an indexed registry and in a layout registry, and not in a per-package git registry without an index**, where listing versions is a tag list and finding the template would cost one fetch per tag: such a registry reports `template_index_required` naming the registry and the fix (publish an index, or mirror into a layout registry). That is a stated limitation, not a silent fallback.

p.TEMPLATE-IN-A-REPO: **Decided 2026-11-11 — a template package is discoverable and installable in an indexed per-package registry, which is the shape every public user has.** `#TEMPLATE-DISCOVERY` always said so: the per-version index record carries `template`, so one read splits revisions from concrete versions, and the client then "fetches that package version through the ordinary path" and reads `[template]` from it. Only the **directory** half was ever built. A per-package git registry contributes no directory root, so `vibe app versions` fell through to the published versions and `vibe install -g org.vibevm.node/node@lts` answered `no version of … matches 'lts'` — against the real `vibespecs` registry, measured 2026-11-11. The three template packages in public were carried entirely by their concrete publications; a template-only package would have had **no installable version at all**, which `#TEMPLATE-REVISION-NOT-A-VERSION` sharpened by correctly removing the revision rows. **What it costs, and why that is the whole design.** Discovery is the index read the registry was already making, plus **one** `vibe.toml` read at the active revision's tag — a single HTTPS GET on GitHub and GitVerse, one `git archive` elsewhere. Not one read per tag: that is the cost `#TEMPLATE-DISCOVERY` says an index exists to avoid, and it is why a per-package registry **without** an index still reports `template_index_required` rather than guessing from a tag list. A **checkout happens only to render**: the revision's whole tree is the produced version's too, so materialisation needs it and nothing else does — listing versions, lowering a channel and reading a skeleton manifest never check anything out. The manifest is read as **text**, never as a typed `Manifest`, for `#TEMPLATE-DOCUMENT-READING`'s reason. A row the index marks as a revision whose manifest does not declare the flag is a disagreement between index and tree: **the tree wins**, the package reads as having no template, and the disagreement is warned about — the same answer a registry with no index gives, rather than a refusal over metadata. The four call sites of `#TEMPLATE-DOMAIN-SEAM` are the same four, in one module beside the registry, so the two registry shapes differ in how a template is **found** and never in what a listing or an install says about it; a rendered version is inserted into the store exactly as a directory registry inserts one, and its lock provenance is the template record the layer noted, because the hash is what binds and upstream has no such tag. Proven end to end against the real public registry: `vibe app versions org.vibevm.node/node` answers 409 versions with their origins and the `lts` / `lts/lithium` channels, and `vibe install -g org.vibevm.node/node@lts` installs **26.13.1** — a version that exists only as a row in upstream's own index document and was never published as a package — with `node -v` answering `v26.13.1`.

p.TEMPLATE-NO-DIGEST: **Decided 2026-11-11 — a template whose produced versions download nothing declares no digest source, and installs.** `#TEMPLATE-VERSIONS` made `[template.digests]` mandatory, and `TemplateLayer::full` fetched that version's digest document as its **first act** — before it knew whether the manifest named a single `{sha256:…}` or `{size:…}` variable. That is right for every template whose produced versions download an archive, and wrong for the genre this campaign's own shim belongs to: a tool whose release is a file the package itself carries, installed by a `kind = "copy"` step out of the rendered tree. Such a template had to declare a per-version digest document that does not exist, and the install failed fetching it; the *listing* worked, because a skeleton render reads no digests, which is what made the gap invisible until something tried to install. Measured 2026-11-11: a two-file local registry with one `kind = "list"` item and one `copy` step answered `0.41.0 (template)` and then `✗ registry_failed … the digest document … could not be fetched`. **The rule: `[template.digests]` is optional, and a template that declares none may not name a digest variable anywhere.** The refusal is at the variable, not at the table, because only the variable's own site knows it is being used — and it is a refusal rather than the skeleton placeholder, so the failure lands at **resolution** — in the skeleton render, before any effect — with the fix in it, rather than at install time on a lookup into an empty table. The version *listing* is deliberately unaffected either way, because a domain is the version list and renders nothing at all. Nothing weakens: "every downloaded input is digest-verified" holds by there being no downloaded input, and a template that declares a digest source is unchanged in every respect, down to the bytes it serialises. The three records that carried the document's identity learn to say "none" rather than to say nothing: the lock's `digest_source_sha256` becomes optional and the mirror snapshot's `[source].digest_url` and `[[version]].digest_sha256` with it — **absent, never an empty string**, because a provenance record of a document that does not exist is an invention, and `#TEMPLATE-LOCK-RECORD`'s alarm compares the recorded value with the computed one, so an invented one would hide a real change. The lock pays one epoch for that (`AV-FMT-033`, 10 → 11, pinned by name as `DIGESTLESS_TEMPLATE_SCHEMA_VERSION`): a schema-10 reader *requires* the field, so a lock omitting it must claim a higher epoch or be unreadable by the reader its own `schema_version` names — the mirror image of AV-FMT-002's rule for a record `deny_unknown_fields` would refuse. The epoch ladder keeps its shape and its output: `for_write` still writes the lowest epoch that carries what the lock holds, and **no lock written before this changes a byte**, because no template that could produce a digest-less record existed. The installed-application record needed nothing at all — its two digest members have been optional since AV-FMT-017, and one `Some(...)` wrapper in `vibe-app` was the whole distance between them and this.

p.DOWNLOAD-HEADERS: **Decided 2026-11-12 — one invocation may attach extra HTTP request headers to the installer's own downloads, and the command line names a file rather than a value.** `vibe install -g <target> … --download-header-file <path>` reads a file of `Name: value` lines — a `#` comment line and a blank line are skipped — and sends those headers with every `http://` and `https://` input **this install** downloads. It exists because what a mirror behind an authenticating gateway needs is exactly one header, and vibe had no per-invocation header mechanism at all; nvm has carried `$NVM_AUTH_HEADER` for the same reason since its mirror support, and `org.vibevm.nvm/nvm` lowers that variable onto this flag. **The path is the surface and the value never is.** Every local user on the machine can read `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, so a credential in argv is a credential published to the machine; nvm takes this seriously enough to hand the value to curl in a config file on stdin and to GNU Wget in a private `wgetrc`, and to put it on the command line only for BusyBox wget, which reads no config file at all (`nvm.sh`, `nvm_download` and `nvm_wget_with_auth_header`). There is therefore **no flag that takes the value**, and adding one would undo the whole feature. The values are equally absent from everything vibe writes down — not at `-v`, not in a transfer record (`TransferRecord::http` has never had a header field and gains none), not in a failure message, not in `--json`, not in the journal — while the **names** may appear, because they are useful and are not secret: `Debug` on the parsed file prints the names and nothing else, and no refusal variant carries a value. A file that cannot be read, declares no header at all, holds a line that is not `Name: value`, a name that is not an HTTP field name, or a value carrying a control character is refused **by name, with its line number, before the first request of the run**. **It changes nothing about what may be contacted.** A header says what is sent once an endpoint may already be reached; the admission of `PROP-073#HTTP-ADMISSION-LAW` runs first, unchanged, in the same place and in the same order, so an excluded endpoint refuses with the same code and the same text whether or not a header file was given, and refuses before the socket is accepted. It is as deliberately not a global: the headers ride on the installer's fetch of a declared input (`FetchWatch`) rather than on the operation's HTTP client, so a registry read, an index read and a template-document fetch — which share that client — cannot see them, and a `file:` or package-relative source is read rather than requested and gets nothing. A remap row is the one place they do travel, and on purpose: the row is the user's own declaration of where these bytes come from, and behind a gateway it is usually how the mirror is named at all (`PROP-066#locator`). **They belong to one origin.** Against a managed client vibe owns the redirect chain already, so the headers are dropped — beside `Authorization`, `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization`, by the same rule — the moment a hop leaves the origin the fetched URL named, permanently within that chain, so a redirect that comes home does not re-attach them. The direct branch, taken when a fetch was handed no managed client, has no walk of its own, so it **refuses** a redirect out of that origin instead of following it anonymously; that is nvm's own answer (`nvm_wget_same_origin`, which stops GNU Wget at every redirect and declines a cross-origin one, "wget would send $NVM_AUTH_HEADER there too"), and it is a refusal rather than a silent strip because a credential that quietly becomes an anonymous request reads as a mirror that forgot its gateway. A request carrying these headers is therefore always issued on a pool that follows no redirect by itself; a pool that does refuses to carry them, so the rule cannot be bypassed by reaching for the wrong client. Nothing else of the incumbent unbound HTTP policy moves with it — the proxy route, the trust set and the timeout are the ones that run without the flag.

p.TEMPLATE-REVISION-NOT-A-VERSION: **Decided 2026-11-11 — a template revision is never a candidate, on every shape of registry.** `#TEMPLATE-FLAG` says the package's own `version` is the revision of the template and not a version of what it produces, and `#TEMPLATE-DISCOVERY` says an indexed client splits the rows by the `template` boolean the record carries. The **directory-shaped** path did exactly that from the start (`discover_in_directory` splits the manifests on disk, and `union_versions` removes the revisions from the published set), so `LocalRegistry::list_versions` never listed one and `LocalRegistry::resolve`, which picks out of that same list, never selected one. The **indexed** path did not: `VersionEntryView`, the registry client's hand-written partial decode of a `by-name` row, had no `template` field at all, so serde dropped the flag the index was already writing, and `GitPerPackageRegistry` listed and selected a revision like any other version. Measured 2026-11-11 against the public `vibespecs` registry: `vibe app versions org.vibevm.node/node` answered five rows, of which `1.1.0 (published)` and `1.0.0 (published)` were the template's own revisions; `org.vibevm.opencode/opencode` and `org.vibevm.qwen/qwen-code` carried three and one more. Nothing had broken yet only because every revision happened to sort **below** the package's newest produced version, so `@latest` was accidentally right — but `@^1`, `@1.1.0` and `@~0.0` each selected a revision, `vibe outdated` could report one as an update, and a package whose revisions outrank its produced versions — which is exactly `org.vibevm.nvm/nvm`, revisions `1.x` against nvm's `0.41.x` — would have had every selection land on the template itself. **The rule, now true on both shapes: a template revision is neither listed nor selectable.** No format changed — the index has carried `template` on every row since AV-FMT-003 and the writer has always written it; what changed is that the client now reads it. The flag is read where it arrives, and the split is applied once, in `list_candidates_with_route`, above both the listing and the selector, so the two cannot disagree; naming a revision exactly refuses with `NoMatchingVersion`, the same refusal the directory path already gave. Three things deliberately keep seeing revisions, because each reads one by identity rather than selecting it: template **discovery** itself, which reads the newest revision's tree; a **mirror**, which must copy the revision or stop carrying the template package (its index-backed listing reads `primary.jsonl` directly and its tag-backed listing goes through the git path, so neither is filtered); and a **lock**, which records the revision as provenance beside the produced version and replays by the rendered hash, never by resolving `@<revision>`. The **tag-list fallback** — a per-package git registry with no index — carries no manifest and so cannot tell the two apart; it declares nothing rather than guessing, which is the same honest shortfall `#TEMPLATE-DISCOVERY` already records for that registry shape, and templates do not work there at all.

p.TEMPLATE-DOMAIN-SEAM: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the exact seam by which a template's version domain enters the resolver.** The resolver already has one enumeration seam and one manifest seam: `VersionEnumerator::list_versions(&self, group, name)` (`crates/vibe-resolver/src/lib.rs`) and `DepProvider::fetch_manifest(&self, group, name, version)` (same file). Neither is touched. Both are implemented, for every production path, by `MultiRegistryDepProvider` over `MultiRegistryResolver`, and `vibe install -g` reaches the same `MultiRegistryResolver` through `vibe_package_source::build_install_resolver_with_operation` and `resolver.resolve_and_fetch` (`crates/vibe-app/src/resolve.rs` `from_global_with_operation`), so one place serves project resolution and global application installation alike. The template layer is therefore one new module `crates/vibe-registry/src/templates.rs` wired at exactly four call sites: `MultiRegistryResolver::list_versions_in_registry` (`…/multi_registry_resolver/walk.rs`) unions the published versions, minus the template revisions, with the source's versions; `MultiRegistryResolver::fetch_manifest_inner` (`…/walk/manifest.rs`) returns a skeleton render for a version the source produces and the registry does not publish; `MultiRegistryResolver::resolve` / the store-backed fetch materialises a **full** render as an ordinary package directory under `<cache>/templates/rendered/<group>/<name>/v<version>/` — the template's tree copied with its `vibe.toml` replaced — and hands back the ordinary `ResolvedPackage` / `CachedPackage` every caller already expects; and `LocalRegistry::{list_versions, resolve}` (`crates/vibe-registry/src/local_registry.rs`) does the same for `--registry DIR`. Below those four sites nothing in the resolver, the SAT engine, the planner or `vibe-app` learns that a manifest was rendered: a rendered version is a package directory like any other, which is what keeps the blast radius at one module.

p.TEMPLATE-CONCRETE-WINS: **Decided 2026-11-10 — mechanics of "concrete wins".** The version domain is the union of the two sets; for a version in both, the published package is resolved and fetched and **the template is not rendered for it at all** — not rendered and compared, not rendered and discarded. That makes hand-fixing one version free of any digest fetch and makes the fix total: a published `org.vibevm.node/node@24.22.2` may differ from what the template would have produced in every field. `vibe app versions` marks each version `template` or `published`, and a version in both is marked `published (overrides template)`. A published version that is byte-identical to the rendering is not detected and not reported: that would cost a digest fetch per version to answer a question nobody asked.

p.TEMPLATE-LOCK-RECORD: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the lock and installation-record fields, and the alarm.** `LockedPackage` (`crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/lockfile.rs`) gains one optional table `template` holding `revision` (the template package's own version), `rendered_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the full render's TOML bytes), `digest_source_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the fetched digest document's bytes) and `source_url` / `digest_url` as they were resolved after remap, plus — beside it, on `LockedPackage` itself — one optional `via_channel` naming the channel the requirement was lowered through (`#CHANNEL-SYNTAX`). The lockfile's internal `schema_version` goes 9 → 10 and `admit` accepts 7–10, following the precedent of the 7→8→9 steps, which did not bump the format registry's own epoch. The application installation record (`crates/vibe-app/src/index.rs` `Installation`) gains the same `template` table, which moves the inventory to protocol `vibe-user-applications/7` (`#FORMAT-CHANGES`). **The alarm**: before a locked or recorded version is installed, updated, reinstalled or modified, the full render is recomputed and its `rendered_sha256` compared with the recorded one; a difference refuses the operation before any effect with code `template_render_changed`, naming the package, the version, the template revision then and now, the recorded and the computed hash, and — computed from the two renders — the exact digest-bearing fields that differ. There is no `--trust-template` flag: the two legitimate causes each have an honest answer, re-locking (`vibe update`, which rewrites the record deliberately) or a concrete publication of that version (`#TEMPLATE-CONCRETE-WINS`), and the escape hatch PROP-002 `#TRUST-MIRROR-HATCH` provides for a mirror is about availability, which this is not. A change of the *template revision* alone, with the same produced version and the same digests, is not an alarm: the recorded `revision` is updated in place with a note, because TEMPLATE-FLAG's whole purpose is that a template can be fixed without touching a produced version — the hash is what binds, not the revision.

p.TEMPLATE-CACHE: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the offline cache and its staleness rule.** One directory per template package under the settings root, beside the caches PROP-059 `#source-build` and PROP-065 `#execution` already own: `<settings>/cache/templates/<group>/<name>/`, holding `versions.json` (a small envelope: the source url after remap, the fetched bytes' SHA-256, the RFC 3339 fetch time, and the fetched document verbatim), `digests/<version>` (the digest document verbatim) and `rendered/v<version>/` (the materialised package directory of `#TEMPLATE-DOMAIN-SEAM`). **Staleness is asymmetric because the two documents are.** A digest document of a released version is immutable: it is cached forever, never revalidated, and a changed one upstream is precisely the alarm of `#TEMPLATE-LOCK-RECORD` — so caching it forever is what makes the alarm meaningful rather than a race. A version list is mutable: it is refetched when the cached copy is older than `[template] version_list_ttl` in `~/.vibe/config.toml` (default **15 minutes**), and otherwise read from the cache, so a shell prompt hook and a loop of `vibe app exec` cost no network at all. `--refresh` on any command that resolves refetches it regardless; `--offline`, `VIBE_OFFLINE` and `[net] offline` read the cache whatever its age and refuse a miss with `template_cache_missing`, naming the package, the exact cache path and the command that would fill it. **A requirement already satisfied by the lock never fetches the version list**, because the lock names the version; a locked install is one digest request, or zero when the rendered directory is still cached. Every fetch is an ordinary transfer of PROP-068 `#transfer` through the operation's controlled transport and the remap Locator (PROP-066 `#locator`), so a closed network redirects a template's sources with the rows it already uses and `vibe remap explain` answers for them; the two new artifact kinds this needs are in `#FORMAT-CHANGES`.

p.CHANNEL-SYNTAX: **Decided 2026-11-10 — channel syntax, and how it lowers.** A channel name is `[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*`, optionally one `/` and a second such segment (`lts`, `lts/jod`, `nightly`); it is written where a version requirement is written, after the `@` (`org.vibevm.node/node@lts`, `node@lts/jod`), and in a version file. `VersionSpec` (`crates/vibe-core/src/package_ref.rs`) gains a third variant `Channel(ChannelName)`; `VersionSpec::parse` tries `semver::VersionReq` first and only a string that fails that **and** matches the channel grammar becomes a channel, so no existing requirement changes meaning. Two channel names are reserved and implemented by vibe for every package, template or not, with the meaning PROP-019 `#selectors` already gives them: `latest` is the newest version in the domain and `stable` the newest non-prerelease. **A channel names a version set and lowers to the newest member of that set as an exact pin, before the solve.** That is what `nvm install --lts` means and it keeps the solver untouched: `SemverVersionSet::from_spec` maps an unlowered channel to the empty set, so a path that forgot to lower fails closed with "no candidate" instead of resolving something plausible, and `VersionSpec::matches` of a channel is `false` with the invariant stated at the call site. Lowering is one named function `lower_channel(&mut PackageRef, &dyn ChannelResolver)` called at exactly the entry paths that accept a requirement — `vibe install` / `update` of a project requirement, `vibe install -g` / `update -g`, `vibe app use`, `vibe app exec`, `vibe app versions`, the version-file reader and the mirror's selection — each with a test that the unlowered form reaches nothing. A template's channels are declared as `[[template.channel]]` rows, each with `from` (a field of the version record) and exactly one of two rules: `rule = "truthy"` with `name` (every version whose field is truthy is a member — Node's `lts`), or `rule = "value"` with `prefix` (one channel per distinct field value, named `<prefix>/<value lower-cased>` — Node's `lts/jod`). For a **concrete** package a channel is a publisher-assigned label: `[package] channels = ["lts"]` in its own manifest, carried into the per-version index record, so resolving a concrete channel is an index read and never a scan of every manifest; a registry without an index refuses a concrete channel with `template_index_required`, the refusal of `#TEMPLATE-DISCOVERY`. **The lock records the concrete version and `via_channel`**, so `vibe.toml` keeps saying `lts` while `vibe.lock` says `24.22.2` and `vibe update` re-lowers — the same split the file and the lock already have for `^22`.

mirror.title: 3. Templates in mirrors and closed networks

p.MIRROR-TEMPLATE-SNAPSHOT: A mirror copies the template package itself plus a snapshot of its external data restricted to the selected versions (their source records and digests), kept under the target's `_index/`. A client inside the closed network renders a selected version locally from that snapshot with the same code as outside; the mirror never writes thousands of rendered package directories. The snapshot is part of the mirror commit, so its digests are fixed there.

p.MIRROR-CONFIG: `vibe registry mirror --config mirror.toml` reads a declarative selection: `[select]` for ordinary packages (`all`, groups, packages, excludes) and one `[[template]]` per template package (version requirements, channels, `newest = N` per major, the installer options/platforms wanted, whether payloads are fetched, and how much of the version list the snapshot carries). Command-line selection flags override it. The selection is recorded beside the mirror provenance (`_index/mirrors/<source>.toml`), so a later run without `--config` repeats it and adds only what newly matches; a reverse mirror reads the same record.

p.MIRROR-NO-SILENT-PRUNE: Narrowing a selection never deletes: versions are immutable and a project may have locked one. Removal is explicit (`--prune`) and shown as a plan first.

p.MIRROR-PAYLOAD-BUDGET: With payloads selected, the mirror fetches the inputs of the selected versions and platforms into the package drop at the paths the drop lookup already reads. `--dry-run` shows the projection with counts and total bytes; a `[payloads] max_total` budget stops the run before writing and names what does not fit.

p.MIRROR-CONFIG-SCHEMA: **Decided 2026-11-10 — `mirror.toml`.** One authored TOML document, `schema = 1`, refused outright when `schema` is anything else, exactly as `_index/mirrors/<source>.toml` is today (`crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/registry/mirror/record.rs`). `[select]` carries `all` (boolean, default `false`), `groups` (array of group ids), `packages` (array of `group/name`) and `exclude` (array of either), which generalises today's `Filters` (`mirror.rs`, `--package` / `--group`, no excludes) to the same two axes plus a subtraction; `all = false` with no groups and no packages selects nothing and is a usage refusal, never a silent empty run. One `[[template]]` row per template package carries `package` (`group/name`, required), `versions` (an array of version requirements, ORed), `channels` (an array of channel names), `newest` (an integer N: for every major version present after the other filters, keep the newest N — the one selector a human actually wants), `platforms` / `archs` (arrays of vibe platform and architecture ids), `installers` (an array of installer-option ids, which wins over `platforms` / `archs` when given) `payloads` (boolean, default `false`) and `version_list` (`"all" | "selected"`, default `all`). **`version_list`, decided 2026-11-12 on the owner’s «обрезать список».** The snapshot’s `versions.json` is the document a client’s whole version domain and channel table are computed from, so it is what decides which versions a closed network can see and resolve at all. `all` restricts it to **every** version the snapshot’s record names, accumulated over every run, which is the behaviour before the key existed and therefore the default: a client parses one document, so a re-run that narrowed it would take away versions the record still names. `selected` restricts it to the versions **this row** selects, so narrowing `versions` / `channels` / `newest` immediately narrows what every client behind the mirror resolves within — the knob a closed network sets so `install -g node@22` cannot land on a version the mirror deliberately did not carry. The document is rewritten in place on every run and never deleted, so the key takes effect in **both** directions by itself and needs no `--prune`; the **digest** files keep following the record rather than the trimmed list, so flipping back to `all` needs no repair run to make those versions usable again. Channels are not stored in a snapshot — a client recomputes them from the version document by the same `[[template.channel]]` rules — so trimming the document trims the channel table with it, and the run’s own projection reports the **trimmed** channel resolution, never the source’s, so the row an operator reads and the table a client computes cannot disagree. The key is recorded in `[[select.template]]` like every other, skipped at its default so every record written before it existed stays byte-identical. A row selecting nothing is reported, not an error. `[payloads]` carries `max_total` (a byte budget written as `"40 GiB"` or an integer) and `into` (the directory payloads are written to; the default is the first configured `[artifacts] packages` drop, and writing payloads into the registry target is **refused by name**, because a monorepo must not grow forty gigabytes). Command-line `--package` / `--group` override `[select]` wholesale rather than intersecting with it, the rule MIRROR-CONFIG states; a `--config` naming a file that does not exist is a refusal. The effective selection — merged from the file and the flags — is written into `_index/mirrors/<source>.toml` as a new `[select]` table and `[[template]]` rows beside the existing `[source]`, `[sync]` and `[[version]]`, so a later bare `vibe registry mirror <source> --into <target>` repeats it and adds only what newly matches. That record's `schema` stays 1: the new tables are additive and a reader that ignores them behaves as today.

p.MIRROR-SNAPSHOT-LAYOUT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the snapshot layout and its staleness rule.** Under the target registry root: `_index/templates/<group>/<name>/snapshot.toml` (`schema = 1`) plus `_index/templates/<group>/<name>/versions.json` and `_index/templates/<group>/<name>/digests/<version>`. `versions.json` is the source document **restricted to the selected versions** — the same envelope `#TEMPLATE-CACHE` caches, with the record array filtered and nothing else altered, so a client parses it with the same `select` the template declares. `digests/<version>` is the upstream digest document for that version, verbatim. `snapshot.toml` records `[source]` (the template coordinate and revision, the version-list url and the digest url template as the template declares them, before remap), `[sync]` (the writing vibe and the first and last sync time, as the mirror record's own `[sync]` does), and one `[[version]]` per snapshotted version with `version`, `digest_sha256` (of the digest document bytes) and `rendered_sha256` (the full render the mirror computed while it was there, so a client inside the network can compare without rendering first, and a mirror operator sees a diff in the commit). The snapshot is written inside the mirror's single commit, through the same `BatchConfig.files` channel the provenance record already uses, so MIRROR-TEMPLATE-SNAPSHOT's "its digests are fixed there" is the git commit itself. **Staleness**: a client reading a snapshot never revalidates it and never contacts the upstream — a snapshot is a frozen version list by construction, which is the whole point in a closed network — and `vibe app versions` reports the snapshot's `[sync] last` beside the versions so a user can see how old the list is and ask the operator to re-run the mirror. A re-run adds versions and leaves existing ones untouched; a `digest_sha256` that changed for an already-snapshotted version is the **alarm** of `#TEMPLATE-LOCK-RECORD` raised at mirror time, stopping the run before anything is written, exactly as PROP-002 `#MIRROR-RULES` stops on a changed hash of a frozen version. `_index/templates/` is a new directory under the registry's `_index/`, which the index writer's ownership whitelist must learn about (`WRITER_DIRS` in `crates/vibe-index/src/index/mod.rs`) and `repomd.json` must list among its `files`, as it lists `by-name/` today.

p.MIRROR-PAYLOAD-PROJECTION: **Decided 2026-11-10.** With `payloads = true` on a `[[template]]` row, the mirror renders each selected version fully, reads the inputs of the selected installer options from the rendered manifest (`steps[].source` with its `sha256`, and `sources[]` inputs), fetches each one through the operation's controlled transport, verifies it against the digest the render produced, and writes it into the drop at the **first** rung of the lookup PROP-066 `#drops` already reads — `<into>/<group>/<name>/<version>/<file>`, where `<file>` is the last path segment of the declared URL, the rung `crates/vibe-core/src/remap/drop.rs` `package_lookup` tries first. Nothing new is invented: the drop is the one artifact-byte mechanism (PROP-066 `#drops`, CORP-FMT-003), the digest is verified as it always is, and the file a client finds there is the file a client would have downloaded. An input already present with the right digest is skipped and counted as present; one present with a wrong digest stops the run with `digest_mismatch` and is not replaced, because a human put it there. Payload projection is the one part of a mirror run that writes outside the registry target, which is why `[payloads] into` is explicit and a missing drop configuration is a refusal naming `[artifacts] packages`.

p.MIRROR-DRY-RUN-OUTPUT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — what `--dry-run` prints and what the budget stops.** The existing dry run lists one decision per version (`copied` / `updated` / `unchanged` / `snapshot-differs` / `alarm` / `unavailable`) and writes nothing; it gains, for each `[[template]]` row, the template coordinate and revision, the count of versions the row selected with the first and last of them, the channels that resolved and to what, the installer options kept per version and the rows dropped by `template_optional`, and — when `payloads` is set — the input count, the bytes already present in the drop, the bytes to fetch and the total, with a flag for every input of unknown size (a Node template declares no `size`, so the total is a lower bound and says so). `[payloads] max_total` is checked against the bytes-to-fetch **before the first byte is written**; over budget stops the run with `payload_budget_exceeded`, naming the budget, the projected total and the versions and platforms that do not fit, in selection order, so narrowing the row is mechanical. The mirror report (`schemas/registry_mirror_report.jtd.json`) gains a `templates[]` array carrying the same facts, and its `dry_run` member already exists. The human form is drawn in PROP-067's display language, as the plan of PROP-065 `#plan` is: one node per template row, its versions as children.

p.MIRROR-PRUNE: **Decided 2026-11-10.** `--prune` is a separate verb-like flag on `vibe registry mirror` that removes what the **recorded** selection no longer matches: package versions under the target's `<group>/<name>/v<version>/`, snapshot versions under `_index/templates/`, and — only with `--prune-payloads` — files under the drop. It is always a two-step: the plan is printed first (one row per removal with its reason, "no longer selected by `[[template]]` org.vibevm.node/node") and nothing is removed without `--yes` in an unattended run or a yes in an attended one; `--dry-run --prune` prints the plan and stops. A version any `[[version]]` row of `_index/mirrors/<source>.toml` records as copied from a *different* source is never pruned by this source's run. A pruned version's index rows and its journal facts are rewritten in the same commit as the removal, so the target is never left advertising bytes it no longer has. The removal is reported in the mirror report as a new `pruned[]` array. MIRROR-NO-SILENT-PRUNE's law is unchanged: no run without `--prune` ever deletes anything, however narrow the selection became.

p.VERSIONS-LIST: `vibe app versions PACKAGE|SLOT` lists the available versions (template-produced and published), the installed ones, the default and the channels.

p.VERSION-FILES: A package may declare version files it understands, from a closed set of formats: a plain version file (`.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `.python-version`, `.java-version` and the like, named by the package) and the asdf `.tool-versions` format with the package's key. In a project, the project's `vibe.toml` requirement on the application decides first; a declared version file is read when no requirement exists.

p.ACTIVATION: Beside `vibe shell`: `vibe app env --use SLOT=VER` prints the lines that switch the current shell (bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell; a `for /f`-usable form for cmd), and `vibe hook bash|zsh|fish|pwsh` installs a prompt hook that applies the project's versions on directory change, cached by file modification time. cmd has no prompt hook; there `vibe shell` remains the way.

p.VERSION-EXEC: `vibe app exec SLOT@VER -- COMMAND …` runs one command with that version first on PATH, without changing defaults or the shell.

p.MIGRATION: `vibe app migrate SLOT FROM TO` moves an application's user state between two installed versions, and is offered (never run without consent) when a slot gains a new version or its default changes. The strategy comes from the package: `[[application.migration]]` entries with an `export` step run by the old version and an `import` step run by the new one, executed as ordinary recipe steps (interpreters, needs, display, cancellation, run records), with both installations' roots and versions and a shared work directory passed in. Examples: Node re-installs global npm packages; a JDK carries an imported corporate CA from the old `cacerts` into the new one; Python carries user packages.

p.VERSIONS-LIST-OUTPUT: **Decided 2026-11-10, amended 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12.** `vibe app versions PACKAGE|SLOT [PATTERN] [--channel NAME] [--installed] [--in-drop] [--limit N] [--all] [--refresh] [--registry DIR] [--json]`. **`PATTERN` is the version filter nvm's `ls <pattern>` and `ls-remote <pattern>` are**, and it is read by exactly the rule `#VERSION-FILE-VALUE` gives a version file's value — a complete version is itself, a partial one is a prefix, a channel name narrows as `--channel` does, and any other spelling is the requirement it already is — so one rule answers "which versions does this spelling mean" wherever a user writes one. It narrows both the installed listing and the available one, the human rows and `--json` alike, before the limit is applied, so `total`, `shown` and `more` describe the narrowed set. A spelling that is neither a version pattern nor a channel is the refusal `bad_version_pattern`, and a channel the package does not declare is the same `unknown_channel` refusal `--channel` gives, because a typo must not read as an empty domain; both land before any version is listed. **An `@VER` suffix on the target is the same filter**: `vibe app versions 'org.vibevm.node/node@22'` used to be accepted and then silently ignored, and now means what it says. The argument is a `group/name` coordinate or a slot id; a slot with providers from several packages lists each package's versions under its own heading, and an ambiguous bare name is the ordinary refusal that names the spellings, never a guess. One row per version, newest first, carrying the version, its origin (`template`, `published`, or `published (overrides template)`), the channels it belongs to, and its local state (`installed`, `installed (default)`, `installed (hidden)`, `installed (held)`, or empty), with a trailer naming the slot, its default, whether the slot is off, and — in a closed network — the snapshot's `[sync] last` of `#MIRROR-SNAPSHOT-LAYOUT`. Without `--all` the newest 20 are shown with a count of the rest, because Node's domain is 878 records. `--json` answers `vibe-app-versions/1` (`schemas/application_versions.jtd.json`) with the same facts plus the resolved channel table and, for a template, the template coordinate, revision and version-list fetch time. The command resolves and **renders nothing**: it is the skeleton path of `#TEMPLATE-TWO-STAGE` and costs at most one HTTP request, and none at all within the version-list TTL or under `--offline`. **Amended 2026-11-12 on the owner's «давай сделаем это»: a row says whether this machine can install it here and now.** A user in a closed network does not ask which versions exist — they ask which of them they can install today, and the answer is on their own disk. So a row an `[artifacts] packages` drop (PROP-066 `#drops`) **already holds the payload of** carries the mark `in drop`, and `--in-drop` keeps only those rows. The rule, in the order it is decided. **(1)** The inputs are the ones the installer option an unattended install would select **on this host** downloads — the detected platform and architecture, no chooser, so a target with several installers to pick between is unmarked rather than marked for an option nobody has chosen; their file names are the last URL segment of each downloaded `[[sources]]` input and of each `archive` / `native` step, and the `file` an author-side `drop = "packages"` input names (`#drops-author`). The names come out of the **skeleton** render of `#TEMPLATE-TWO-STAGE` and a published version's own manifest on disk (`#TEMPLATE-CONCRETE-WINS`: a concrete version is read, never rendered), reusing the template and version records the domain read already captured, so marking **every** row of Node's domain costs no HTTP request, no digest document, no render into a store and no second registry walk. A name the skeleton cannot settle is **unknown** and the row is unmarked, never guessed; a digest-bearing name cannot arise at all, because a digest variable is legal only in the digest-bearing fields. The one knowable gap is a `template_optional` row, which a full render drops on a missing digest and a skeleton keeps — in practice harmless, because upstream not publishing that file is also why a drop would not hold it. **(2)** The drop is searched **by name alone**: `<drop>/<group>/<name>/<version>/<file>`, then `<drop>/<group>/<name>/<file>`, then `<drop>/<file>` — install's own convention minus the `<drop>/<sha256>/<file>` rung, which a listing has no digest document to build and must not invent; a payload filed only there is served by every fetch as before and simply goes unmarked. Existence and regular-file only: **no byte of a payload is read and nothing is hashed**, because archives are 30–100 MB and integrity stays the install's job, where the digest is known and a wrong file is `#drops`' `digest_mismatch`. Any configured drop may serve the mark, highest layer first. **(3)** A row is marked only when **every** input of the selected option is found, since half a payload installs nothing; an option that downloads nothing is unmarked, there being no file for a drop to hold. **(4)** `--in-drop` narrows **before** the limit, exactly as `PATTERN` does, so `total`, `shown` and `more` describe the narrowed set, and without it the probe is asked only about the rows actually shown. **(5)** Human output puts the mark in the one trailing `— …` segment the local state already uses, comma-separated (`— installed (held), in drop`), and marks an installed row too, because it is a fact about the drop rather than about installability. `--json` carries the found paths as the optional per-row member `drop`, additive and omitted when absent, so an older reader is unaffected (`AV-FMT-107`). **(6)** No drop configured is no mark and **no error**; `--in-drop` without one is the refusal `no_package_drop` naming `[artifacts]` `packages`, because an empty listing would read as an empty domain. `--in-drop` with `--installed` is refused by the parser: `--installed` answers from this home and the template cache alone, with no registry and therefore no manifest to take a file name from, so there is nothing for the filter to narrow.

p.VERSIONS-CHANNEL-DISCOVERY: **Decided 2026-11-11, after the corporate proof measured the asymmetry.** A listing's **channel table, origins and template provenance come from a discovered template, and a template is discovered over a directory root** — so which configured registries contribute a root decides what `vibe app versions` can say, and it must decide the same thing for every spelling of the argument. The proof found it deciding two different things in one home: `vibe app versions node --installed --all` showed `[lts, lts/krypton]`, while `vibe app versions org.vibevm.node/node --channel lts` answered `unknown_channel … channels: (none)` — and the versions were right in both, which is what made it hard to see. The cause was not the argument at all: `--installed` answers from the template **cache**, which an install had primed, while every other path enumerated the roots of the configured chain and that enumeration knew only `localdir`. A **`monorepo` registry is a directory-shaped registry too** — one repository laid out `<group>/<name>/v<version>/`, whose working copy is what every other call site already reads it through — and in the corporate shape it is the *only* registry, so a closed network had no directory root at all and every listing fell back to the published version union: no channels, every row `published`, no provenance and no snapshot line. Two consequences are now facts. **(1)** The roots enumeration asks the **registry layer** which sources have a directory root, per variant and beside the variants, so a kind of registry cannot be silently left out of it; `localdir` offers its own directory, `monorepo` offers its working copy, a per-package **git** registry offers none, and under `--offline` a monorepo offers one only when the repository is local, exactly as a resolution under `--offline` reads it. **(2)** A monorepo root is a **capture its source owns** and lives exactly as long as that source, so the enumeration hands back the roots **with the lease that keeps them on disk** and a reader holds it for as long as it reads the trees — the retention `LayoutRoot` already has for the same reason (PROP-073 `#NATIVE-PREPARATION`). Bare paths would have been paths that stop existing when the call returns, which is the second half of the same defect and the half a passing version list hides. `AV-FMT-014`'s answer is unchanged; what changed is that it is now the same answer whether the argument names a coordinate or a slot, and whatever the registry type.

p.VERSION-FILE-FORMATS: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the closed format set and the precedence.** A package declares `[[application.version_file]]` rows, each with `format` and the fields of its format. `format = "plain"` carries `names` (an ordered array of file names the package understands: `[".nvmrc", ".node-version"]`); the file's content is read as its first non-empty, non-comment line, trimmed, with a `#` comment and a CR tolerated, and that line is read by `#VERSION-FILE-VALUE` below — `lts/jod` in a `.nvmrc` lowers through `#CHANNEL-SYNTAX` exactly as `@lts/jod` does, which is what makes nvm's own `.nvmrc` idiom work unchanged. `format = "tool-versions"` carries `key` (the package's key in asdf's `.tool-versions`: `nodejs`); the file is parsed as whitespace-separated `<key> <version>…` lines, `#` comments ignored, and the **first** version listed for the key is taken, the rest reported as unused. Nothing else is a format: a `.python-version` is a `plain` row, a `package.json` `engines` field is not read at all, and a package needing more waits for a fact amending this one. **Precedence, highest first**: an explicit `--use SLOT=VER` or `SLOT@VER` on the command; the project's `vibe.toml` requirement on that application package; the nearest declared version file, searched from the working directory upward and stopping at the project root (or at the filesystem root outside a project), the declaration order of the `names` array breaking a tie inside one directory; the slot's global default; and a slot that is off, which is none of the above and stays off. That ordering is VERSION-FILES' own rule — the requirement decides first, the file is read when no requirement exists — with the search and tie-break made explicit. **Decided 2026-11-11: the precedence binds `vibe install -g` too, and by the same discovery.** `vibe install -g <group>/<name>` with no version resolves the version from the nearest declared version file and **says which file decided**, because a version the user did not type must never arrive unannounced; with no such file it keeps the behaviour it had, which is the newest the domain offers. The apparent chicken-and-egg — a package's declared version files are known only once the package is resolved, and resolving it needs a version — does not arise, because the discovery is the one an activation already uses: the home's own sidecar of declared rows (`#VERSION-FILE-FORMATS`' `applications/version-files.json`), which records what every **installed** application declares. So the file is consulted exactly when this home already has a provider of that package's slot, which is exactly when the question "what does this project want" has an answer, and a first install of a package the home has never held resolves as it always did. A spelling that already carries an `@` is never second-guessed. `AV-FMT-106`. A version file naming a version that is not installed is **not** an error for a listing or a prompt hook: it is reported as `not installed` with the exact `vibe install -g` command, because a prompt hook must never install anything and must never fail a `cd`. The resolution is cached by the modification time and size of every file consulted in `<home>/cache/version-files.json`, which is what ACTIVATION's "cached by file modification time" names.

p.VERSION-FILE-VALUE: **Decided 2026-11-11 on the owner's requirement that this be general for any SDK switcher, with nvm parity proven — a version file's value means what every switcher's version file means, and that is not what a command line means.** A version file is a record of a choice; a command line is a request to choose. So a value in a declared version file — of **every** format, `plain` and `keyed` alike — is read by one rule, on **every** reader (the activation of `vibe app env` and the prompt hook, `vibe app exec` with no `@VER`, and `vibe install -g` with no version): a value that is a **complete** version, carrying every component a package's versions have (`22.9.0`, optionally `v`-prefixed, a semver pre-release and build included), selects **exactly that version** and never a newer one; a **partial** value (`22.9`, `22`) selects the newest installed or available version whose components begin with it; a **channel** name keeps its channel meaning and lowers through `#CHANNEL-SYNTAX`; and every other spelling keeps the ordinary requirement meaning `semver::VersionReq` gives it, so `^22`, `22.x`, `>=20, <23` and an explicit `=22.9.0` are unchanged. Counting components is the whole rule: three is a pin (`=22.9.0`), two is that minor (`~22.9`), one is that major (`^22`). This is what nvm, pyenv, rbenv, asdf and mise all do with the files whose names these rows declare, and it is the only reading under which `#VERSION-FILE-WRITE` is coherent: that flag writes the **resolved** version precisely so the next reader learns what was chosen, and a resolved version that read back as a caret range would give that away again the moment a newer minor appeared. **The CLI spelling is deliberately NOT changed.** `SLOT@VER`, `PKG@VER` and `--use SLOT=VER` stay requirements — `vibe install -g org.vibevm.node/node@22.9.0` still resolves 22.9.0 as `^22.9.0` — because there the user is asking vibe to resolve, and a pin is spelled `@=22.9.0`. The behaviour change this fact makes is therefore bounded to version files and is a real one, recorded as such: a `.nvmrc` holding `22.9.0` used to select the newest 22.x and now pins 22.9.0, and one holding `22.9` used to reach into 22.10 and now stays inside 22.9. `AV-FMT-106`.

p.ACTIVATION-ENV-OUTPUT: **Decided 2026-11-10 — `vibe app env` per shell.** `vibe app env [--use SLOT=VER]… [--project] [--shell bash|zsh|fish|pwsh|cmd|posix] [--unset] [--json]` prints, on stdout and nothing else, the lines that switch the current shell; with no `--use` and `--project` it prints what the project's requirements and version files resolve to. The shell is the caller's parent shell by the detector `vibe self env` already has, and `--shell` overrides it. The existing `Shell` enum with its `export_line` and its three quoting helpers lives in `crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/vvm/env.rs`; it is promoted to a shared module, gains a `Cmd` variant, and is the one place shell syntax is written in the tree. The lines set exactly two things — `PATH`, with this selection's payload directories prepended and the withdrawn slots' link directories removed, composed by the same `compose_path` `vibe shell` uses, and `VIBE_APP_USE` to `SessionChoices::render()` — so `eval "$(vibe app env --use node=22.23.4)"` and `vibe shell --use node=…` put a shell in the identical state, which is the invariant a test asserts directly. Per shell: bash, zsh and `posix` print `export NAME='value';` with POSIX single-quote escaping; fish prints `set -gx NAME 'value';` and `set -e NAME;` for an unset; pwsh prints `$env:NAME = 'value';`; **cmd prints bare `NAME=VALUE` lines with no quoting and no `set` keyword**, the `for /f`-usable form ACTIVATION asks for, and its help shows the one incantation that consumes it (``for /f "usebackq tokens=1,* delims==" %a in (`vibe app env --shell cmd`) do @set "%a=%b"``) — because cmd has no `eval` and a quoted `set` line cannot be fed through a pipe. `--unset` prints the lines that undo the selection, which is nvm's `deactivate`. `--json` answers `vibe-app-env/1` (`schemas/application_env.jtd.json`) with the resolved selection, the composed PATH as an array and the variables as a table, for a client that sets the environment itself instead of printing it.

p.ACTIVATION-HOOK: **Decided 2026-11-10 — the hook mechanism and its cost budget.** `vibe hook bash|zsh|fish|pwsh [--print] [--yes]` writes one managed block (`spec://org.vibevm.world/managed-blocks/flows/managed-blocks/MANAGED-BLOCKS-PROTOCOL#root`) into that shell's rc file — the same mechanism and the same consent PROP-065 `#env-step` already uses for `env.sh`, never a byte outside the block — and `--print` writes it to stdout instead for a user who installs it themselves. The block defines a small shell function registered on `PROMPT_COMMAND` (bash), `precmd` (zsh), `--on-variable PWD` (fish) or the prompt function (pwsh). **The function spawns no process in the common case.** It keeps, in a shell variable, the directory it last resolved and the lines it applied; when `$PWD` is unchanged it returns immediately, builtins only. When `$PWD` changes it walks up with the shell's own `[ -f ]` test looking for the names the installed packages declare — the block is regenerated with that name list whenever the declared set changes, so the walk is a fixed number of builtin tests and not a `vibe` call — and only when a candidate file exists, or when a previously applied selection must be undone, does it call `vibe app env --project --shell X` once and `eval` it. **The budget, as a checkable gate**: zero subprocesses on a prompt in an unchanged directory and on a `cd` into a directory with no candidate version file; at most one `vibe` invocation on a `cd` that has one; and that invocation does no network, no registry call and no index read — it reads the home's index and the version files only — and completes in under 50 ms warm on this machine, which a fixture measures and asserts. vibe's own side caches the resolution by the modification time and size of the files consulted (`#VERSION-FILE-FORMATS`), so a repeated `cd` between two project directories is two cache hits. cmd gets no hook, as ACTIVATION states; `vibe shell` is the way there. A hook never installs, never downloads, never writes the index and never fails the prompt: a version that is not installed prints one line naming the exact install command and leaves the shell as it was.

p.VERSION-EXEC-SPELLING: **Decided 2026-11-10.** `vibe app exec SLOT[@VER] [--project] -- COMMAND [ARG…]`. `VER` is a version, a version requirement or a channel; omitted, the selection is resolved exactly as `#VERSION-FILE-FORMATS` prescribes. The command runs with that installation's `path_dirs` link targets and its proxy directory prepended to PATH and `VIBE_APP_USE` set, through the same `session_dirs` / `SessionChoices` library `vibe shell --use` calls, so the three surfaces cannot drift; the child inherits the standard streams, its exit status passes through unchanged and POSIX signals are forwarded, as a PATH proxy already does. `--` is required before the command, so a flag of the command is never read as vibe's.
